producer_report.summary:
Hestia's sweep now owns six recurring duties and runs each on its cadence. `DUTIES` in hestia.rs lists them, and `docs/design/hestia.md` section 13 has the matching table. A drain start runs error-review and evidence-labels every time. A landing runs the landing duties that are due: code-health every landing, keep-rule every 10 landings, reading-rule-refusals every 5 landings. `athena hestia sweep` runs whatever is due. Each pass that runs at least one duty commits one `athena.hestia-sweep/1` record, with each duty that ran as a check named by its id. A new optional `duty_pass { occasion, landings }` field on the record stores the landing total, and "every N landings" counts from that. Old sweeps still parse and make a duty read as never run. A failed duty is recorded as errored and is due again at the next pass. The design review is read from the code-health baselines, the counter that queues it. `athena status` (text and `--json`) gains a duties section with last run, next due and an OVERDUE mark. `athena hestia last` skips drain-start and landing passes so they don't hide the last full sweep. The landing hook `code_health_after_landing` now goes through the same scheduler. The second landing hook for one landing runs nothing, which a new squash test shows. I ran fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, the policy test and the mirrors test, and every package's tests; all pass. The one `cargo test --locked` run failed in two athena-cli targets, which I fixed. I then ran the per-package tests rather than a second workspace run.

Three things the plan didn't foresee:
- `athena hestia sweep` no longer re-runs the error-review backfill and the evidence-label derivation when they already succeeded. They still run at every drain start. This is the deliberate change the plan accepted so a second sweep runs none.
- The extra records-only sweep commit after each landing broke two history-pinning athena-cli tests, `cutover_fixture` and `trailer_stop`. The commit sat on local main after the landed commit and was replayed after the squash merge as an unattributed commit. The two fixtures (`test_support.rs` and `trailer_stop.rs`) now reset to the landed commit before the pull request, dropping the duty-pass commit so they pin the same history shape as before. I judged this a fixture artefact: in real use that local records commit rides the next pull request.
- The production hook means every landing now adds one records-only commit on local main, as the CHANGELOG states.

criteria_check.criterion: A test in crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs, run by `cargo test -p athena-core`, builds a duty table with a drain-start, a per-landing and an every-N-landings duty. It shows one sweep runs each due duty and records its last run, and a second sweep within the cadence runs none.
criteria_check.evidence: `a_sweep_runs_each_due_duty_records_the_last_run_and_a_second_sweep_runs_none` in hestia.rs builds a three-duty table (DrainStart, EveryLanding, EveryLandings(3)) and calls the production `hestia_sweep_duties` with a logging runner. The first sweep runs all three. A second sweep within the cadence runs none and lists no checks. Landings 1 and 3 run only the duties that are due. Drain-start and landing occasions run only their own duties, and a failed duty is retried. Each committed record is read back and equals the one returned, with `duty_pass` holding the occasion and landing total. It passed in `cargo test -p athena-core --lib`.

criteria_check.criterion: A test in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs, run by `cargo test -p athena-core`, shows the status view flags a duty whose last run is past its cadence as overdue and does not flag a duty within its cadence. It also shows each duty with last run and next due point.
criteria_check.evidence: status.rs tests: `duty_standings_flag_a_duty_past_its_cadence_and_not_one_within_it` covers late versus in-cadence for drain-start, per-landing, every-10 and every-5 duties, a failed attempt, never-run and an old sweep without `duty_pass`. It also asserts last_run and next_due text. `the_design_review_is_counted_from_the_code_health_baseline` covers the design review. `status_shows_each_duty_with_its_last_run_and_next_due_point_and_flags_the_late_ones` goes through `Athena::status()` over a committed sweep and checks `view.duties` and the JSON. All three passed.

It also describes the `athena status` duties section with last run, next due and OVERDUE. It states the extra records-only commit per drain start or landing that runs a duty.

criteria_check.evidence: `HestiaSweep` gains an optional `duty_pass` field (serde default, skipped when absent, `deny_unknown_fields` kept) plus `DutyPass` and `DutyOccasion` in throughput.rs. The test `a_hestia_sweep_with_a_duty_pass_round_trips_and_an_old_sweep_still_parses` in records.rs round-trips the new field through `AnyRecord::parse` and `to_json`, checks the canonical path with `check_record_file`, and checks the three occasion names and `is_duty_pass`. It parses a literal old-format sweep with `duty_pass` None, still refuses a repeated check id, and refuses an unknown field in the pass. `sweep_with` gained `duty_pass: None` and the existing round-trip test still passes.

open_issues: Departure from the plan: test_support.rs (athena-core) and tests/trailer_stop.rs gained a `git reset --hard` to the landed commit before the pull request. Without it the landing hook's sweep commit breaks two history-pinning fixtures. These files were not in the plan.
Departure from the plan: the status renderer for `DutyStanding` was added to display.rs together with a small display test, as the plan listed.

Every landing now adds one records-only commit on local main, and every drain start adds one when it runs a duty. In real use the commit rides the next pull request, but the history check on local main in a fixture will flag it, as the two fixtures showed.

The plan's own words describe the design-review as overdue when no baseline exists at all; I implemented that. A repository that has never had a landing will show the design review and code-health as overdue until the first landing or `athena hestia sweep`.

`hestia.rs` grew by roughly 700 lines (duty block and tests); the code-health file-size check may queue a structural pass for it. The duty code is one contiguous block under its own section header, so a later split is a pure move.
mistakes: My first `cargo test --locked` run was in the background, and I could not read its output, so I had to re-run in pieces to find the failures. I did not repeat the whole-workspace run afterwards.
I wrote the first draft of the records.rs test with a separate helper function for the old JSON, then simplified it.

Cadence behavior for status was written to the plan's rule (design-review is overdue when no code-health baseline exists), so a brand-new repository shows every duty as overdue until the first landing or sweep. That follows the plan, but a reader may find it noisy.
learnings: `Athena::commit_records` always commits on the current branch, so every landing hook that writes a record leaves a records-only commit on local main after the landed commit. `resync_onto_merge` replays it after the squash merge, and `athena check --history` on the local main then reports it as unattributed. Fixtures that run that check have to drop it.
The cutover fixture in `athena_core::test_support` and `trailer_stop.rs` pin the exact history around a landing, so any new records written by the landing hook shows up in them.

`code_health::landings` counts only first-parent commits with both Athena-Job and Athena-Verified-Content trailers, so duty-pass commits, baselines and person fixes are not landings, and a squash that keeps the trailers is one landing.

The producer shell policy denies pipes, redirects, heredocs, and `head`, `tail`, `grep` and `wc`. Background command output lives under /tmp and cannot be Read from the working copy, so run tests in the foreground when the output is needed.
Several athena-cli test targets (`cutover_fixture`, `trailer_stop`, `drain`, `code_health_hooks`) are the ones that catch a new commit after a landing or a drain start.
desires: A way to read the output of a finished background command from inside the working copy, or a policy that allows redirecting test output to a file in the working directory.
A documented list of which athena-cli test targets pin the history shape around a landing, so a change to the landing hook can be checked against them first.
